# A pointer drag of a tab leaves focus on the body after the drop

## Context

#17844's census lists `TabHeaderActionsNL` red. Since #19277 its first error is `:269`: after the drag terminal, no `More tabs` control appears ("the queued projection drains after SortZone restores natural layout"). Measured today on dev `e3d83f1b91` with a probe copy of the spec (headless, `--workers=1`, runtime root bound), reading `document.activeElement` and the gated `previous-tab` action's node count at each step of the arm:

| step | active element | `previous-tab` nodes |
|---|---|---|
| before the mouse-down (after the body card click) | the card | 1 |
| after `mouse.down()` on the last tab | the tab button (`<button role="tab" tabindex="0">`) | 1 |
| 150 ms later | the tab button | 1 |
| after the drag move to the rail | `BODY` | 0 |
| 500 ms after `mouse.up()` | `BODY` | 0 |

Identical at `ab2ae8c73c` (2026-09-05), so this is not a recent regression of the drag. The rest of the arm follows from it: the plugin's `sortDragProjectionQueued` goes `true` mid-drag and `false` 500 ms after the terminal, the drain runs, and it measures a header that fits (three 73 px tabs + the 80 px grown action + a 12 px spacer against a 310 px bar). The arm's mid-drag growth overflows that bar only with the 20 px gated action present.

Control: the same probe with one `card.click()` right after `mouse.up()` (focus back in the container) passes the entire spec on `e3d83f1b91`, growth 80 px and all assertions after `:269` included.

## The Problem

A mouse-down on a tab header focuses its `<button>`. `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone#onDragStart` then hides the dragged original (`itemStyle.visibility = 'hidden'`, `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:972`). The browser moves focus off an element that becomes `visibility: hidden`, so focus lands on the body; `manager.Focus` delivers the leave, the `TabContainer`'s `containsFocus` turns false, and `toolbar.Base#applyContextualActionState` withdraws the focus-gated actions (node-less since #18069). Nothing at the terminal hands focus back: after the drop the user's focus is on the body.

Three consequences:
- A pointer user dragging a tab watches the header's contextual actions vanish mid-drag and stay gone after the drop, although they are still working in that container.
- Keyboard focus is lost after every tab drag; a drop should leave focus on the moved item, as a plain click on it would.
- The census arm cannot witness the drain: its overflow depends on the gated action staying revealed.

History, from the file's log: the arm was authored 2026-08-20 (#17423) while the actions were persistent; focus gating arrived 2026-08-30 (#17875); a withdrawn action stopped taking rail space 2026-09-01 (#18016), which is when this arm's overflow began depending on focus; the `:65` hidden-node read (2026-09-02, #18069) masked it until #19277.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs`: `onDragStart` sets `me.dragComponent = draggedItem` (`:881`) and hides it (`:972`); `processDragEnd` restores the item styles and the dragged component's visibility (`:597`–`:602`), reorders, resets the gesture state and waits one frame (`:647`) before `dragEnd`. No focus handling exists anywhere under `src/draggable` (grep).
- `Neo.component.Base#focus(id, children, preventScroll, modality)` (`src/component/Base.mjs:1458`) routes to `main.DomAccess.focus`; `modality: 'pointer'` suppresses the accidental focus ring, which is what a pointer gesture wants.
- `containsFocus_` (`src/component/Base.mjs:104`) is the worker's reactive view of focus ownership, kept by `manager.Focus`; on the dragged tab it is `true` at drag start (the mouse-down's focusin has settled, see the table).
- `tab/header/Button.mjs` renders `<button role="tab">`; `test/playwright/setup.mjs:165` stubs `Neo.main.DomAccess` for the unit tier.

## The Fix

`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs`:
1. `onDragStart`, beside `:881`: record whether the gesture took focus, `me.dragFocusOwner = draggedItem.containsFocus ? draggedItem : null`.
2. `processDragEnd`, after the one-frame wait at `:647` (the visibility restore has flushed by then): if `dragFocusOwner` is set and not destroyed, `dragFocusOwner.focus(dragFocusOwner.id, false, true, 'pointer')`; clear the field. A cancelled drag restores the same way.

Coverage:
- `test/playwright/unit/draggable/container/SortZone.spec.mjs`: one arm records the stub's `focus` calls, runs a drag start and end for an item with `containsFocus: true` and asserts exactly one call for that item with `modality: 'pointer'`, then the same for an item without focus and asserts none.
- The e2e witness is the census arm itself, unchanged: `TabHeaderActionsNL` passes at the head with the runtime root bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `test/playwright/e2e/tab/TabHeaderActionsNL.spec.mjs`, unchanged, passes `:269` at the head (headless, `--workers=1`, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` bound; CI does not select it) and its first error moves to `:288`, the consistency read that #19282 owns; with #19282 applied the spec passes. Measured after filing: the restored focus sits on the dropped tab, which the overflow projection then withholds, so focus is lost a second time (#19285); that loss does not reach any assertion once #19282 lands.
- [ ] AC-2: the unit arm: a drag whose dragged item owned focus at start ends with one `DomAccess.focus` call for that item, modality `pointer`; a drag whose item did not own focus ends with none; a cancelled drag behaves like a committed one.
- [ ] AC-3: red-first: the unit arm fails on dev, and the e2e spec fails at `:269` on dev, both with the fix reverted.

## Out of Scope

- Keeping the gated actions revealed *during* the drag. That needs either a hiding mechanism the browser does not blur for (`visibility: hidden` is what removes the original from the accessibility tree today) or parking focus on a still-visible node at drag start; a separate call, once the terminal is right.
- `verifyComponentConsistency` reporting a `removeDom` vdom node as a DOM mismatch: #19282. The projection withholding a focused tab and dropping focus to the body: #19285.
- The other #17844 rows.

dragged original at drag start, which moves the browser's focus to the body.
Nothing at the terminal gave it back, so a tab drag left focus on the body and
withdrew the header's contextual actions. The zone records the item as the
focus owner at drag start and, once the item is visible again after the
terminal's frame, focuses it as a pointer focus, committed or cancelled."
